subject: Intermittent 5xx observations from model 'cumulus-x' — timeline & verification request
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@helixhealth.com>; support@helixhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 5xx observations from model 'cumulus-x' — initial notice

Hi Sam —

We observed an uptick in 5xx responses for requests routed to the cumulus-x model in your production pool starting ~2028-03-16 07:50 PDT. Early signs: short, bursty windows (~2–4 minutes) of increased 5xx rate (~6–10% of token-generation requests) followed by normal behavior after automated fallback kicked in.

What we're doing now:
- Rolling collection of per-request traces and KV cache metrics (attached: aggregated metrics CSV).
- Automatic routing fallback to cumulus-x-quant-v2 for affected requests.
- Throttling transient retry bursts to protect downstream latency.

Can you confirm whether you saw any client-side retries or application errors on your end in that timeframe? Any sample request IDs would help (we include a few request IDs in the attached CSV correlated to your account).

We want to be transparent and keep you updated; I'll send another note once we have an initial root-cause hypothesis or if we need a short maintenance window.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:05:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx observations from model 'cumulus-x' — initial notice

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the heads-up.

We saw intermittent HTTP 502/504 responses in our logs around 07:52–08:03 and again at 08:27. Those requests are part of a background inference pipeline with light retries (two attempts). I pulled three request IDs from our logs that match timestamps: HLX-req-6a7f, HLX-req-6a8c, HLX-req-6b12.

Impact: roughly 0.8% of inference calls for the last hour failed and were retried by our queue; one downstream job timed out and required manual restart. Not a full outage yet, but we'll need SLA credits if this pattern persists.

Happy to join a short sync if you want to review traces together.

— Sam
Director of Platform Engineering
Helix Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:22:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent 5xx observations from model 'cumulus-x' — initial notice

Looping in ops notes and next steps:

- Observed correlated increase in KV cache misses in the cumulus-x replication group around 07:50 PDT; cache pressure spike due to an atypical long-context workload (2500–3500 tokens) from a small customer cohort.
- Fallbacks were triggered correctly; latency spike before fallback caused upstream HTTP gateways to produce 502/504s for some short-lived connections.
- Immediate mitigation applied: committed temporary request-size cap for cumulus-x routes (limit: 2048 tokens) and progressive drain of long-context traffic to the quantized variant.

Next actions:
1) Ops to run a controlled replay of the long-context traces to reproduce (Grace).
2) Engineering to evaluate memory/attention kernel behavior under 3k+ context and propose a quantization or memory-hint patch (Marissa).
3) Customer comms: Soojin to share an ETA for a validated fix and goodwill credit proposal.

I'll prepare a short internal thread for a postmortem draft.

— Ben
Account Executive (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@helixhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Cumulus-x update: mitigation complete, planned remediation & postmortem draft

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the quick verification and request IDs — that helped us correlate traces. Summary and next steps:

What happened (brief):
- A small set of requests with >2500 token contexts triggered inefficient attention kernel paths in cumulus-x leading to intermittent OOM-like failures at the model-process level. These surfaced as 502/504s at the HTTP gateway during short bursts.

Immediate mitigation (completed 2028-03-16):
- Traffic routing: long-context requests automatically routed to cumulus-x-quant-v2.
- Request cap: applied soft cap at 2048 tokens on cumulus-x production route for 48 hours.
- Autoscale: temporary scale-up of cumulus-x replica counts to reduce queueing latency.

Remediation plan (timeline):
- Week 0–1: Engineering patch to optimize attention kernel selection for >2k contexts (Marissa owner).
- Week 2: Deploy patch to canary, run replay tests with Helix-supplied traces and internal stress tests (Grace owner).
- Week 3: Full rollout with monitoring for error-rate regression and automated rollback.

Goodwill: We propose a one-month credit applied to March usage (details to follow from Ben) and a scheduled verification call next week.

Postmortem draft is attached (cumulusx_postmortem-draft-v1.pdf) — it includes timeline, root cause hypothesis, and proposed mitigations. Please review and let us know any missing items; we'll finalize and share publicly with your engineering leads.

Would you be available for a 30-minute verification call on Tues 2028-03-21 at 10:00AM PDT? If not, suggest an alternative.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
